ei.title: 함축 의미 추론 — 성공의 대가로서의 자유 상실
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고2

fullPassage: Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they’re able to buy. Look instead at what they’re forced to trade in return ― look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don’t like. It will require ― inevitably ― realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well — but they haven’t truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, “Slavery resides under marble and gold.” Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you’re working hard toward? Let’s hope not.

questions.passage: Take a look at some of the most (A)[powerful / powerless], rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they’re able to buy. Look instead at what they’re (B)[forced / allowed] to trade in return ― look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don’t like. It will require ― inevitably ― realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well — but they haven’t truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, “Slavery resides under marble and gold.” Too many successful people are (C)[prisoners / volunteers] in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you’re working hard toward? Let’s hope not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) 강력한 (B) 강요받는 (C) 수감자들 — 성공한 사람들은 강력하지만 특정 행동을 강요받으며 결국 자신이 만든 감옥의 수감자가 된다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① powerless — 원문은 powerful (반의어)
❌ ② allowed — 원문은 forced (반의어)
❌ ③ volunteers — 원문은 prisoners (반의어)
✅ ④ powerful — forced — prisoners: 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: powerful(강력한), forced(강요된), prisoners(수감자) 모두 성공의 대가를 보여주는 핵심 단어

det.korean: 싫어하는 사람들에게 아첨해야 한다 — kissing up to(아첨하는)가 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① kissing up to ←정답 — 좋아하지 않는 사람들에게 아첨하다
❌ ② trade in return — 대가로 거래하다 (다른 문맥)
❌ ③ pay well — 보수가 좋다 (다른 문맥)
❌ ④ wear a suit — 정장을 입다 (다른 문맥)

questions.passage: Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they’re able to buy. Look instead at what they’re forced to trade in return ― look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don’t like. It will require ― inevitably ― realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well — but they haven’t truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, “Slavery resides under marble and gold.” Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you’re __________? Let’s hope not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그것이 당신이 열심히 노력하는 방향인가? — working hard toward(열심히 노력하는)가 적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ① in the world — 세상에서 (다른 문맥)
❌ ② cost them — 그들에게 치르게 한 (다른 문맥)
❌ ③ under marble and gold — 대리석과 황금 아래 (Seneca 인용)
✅ ④ working hard toward ←정답 — 열심히 목표로 하여 일하는
det.tip: work hard toward = ~를 향해 열심히 노력하다
